vitals.title: Process overview band
vitals.desc: Automatic mode collapses the overview band when the window runs out of room.

visibility.title: System process hiding rules
visibility.desc: Customize programs to always show or also hide. Processes and Connections share these rules; use the toolbar icon to enable hiding.

userGroups.title: Group processes by user
userGroups.desc: Automatic mode groups only while more than one user is signed in, including disconnected sessions.

holdOrder.title: Pause sorting while hovering
holdOrder.desc: Readings keep updating; rows re-sort once the pointer leaves the list.

navigation.title: Navigation position
navigation.desc: The side pane shows only icons by default; the ☰ button in its top-left corner expands it.

autostart.title: Start when signing in to Windows
autostart.desc: Starts quietly in the system tray.

startPage.title: Default page
startPage.desc: The page shown when the window first opens after Argus starts.

trayPage.title: Reopen from tray
trayPage.desc: Applies when reopening through the tray or a shortcut.

closeToTray.title: Keep in the system tray when closed
closeToTray.desc: While hidden, history and rules keep working.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.scope: Everyday actions, navigation and list shortcuts.
shortcuts.globalHint: Current setting. Also works while using other apps.
shortcuts.inputHint: In-app shortcuts do not affect other apps. End-process shortcuts are inactive in text fields, dialogs and menus.
shortcuts.search: Go to process search. The / key also works when not typing, and on the Processes page typing a letter or digit starts a search.
shortcuts.runTask: Start a program or open a file or folder from any page. Not while typing.
shortcuts.pause: Hold to pause updates on Processes or Performance; release to return to the previous state.
shortcuts.end: End the selected process or app group, with confirmation.
shortcuts.taskManager: Open Argus when Task Manager replacement is enabled.
shortcuts.expand: Processes: collapse / expand a group or category, or select a parent / child
shortcuts.copyName: Copy the name of the selection
shortcuts.copyDetails: Copy the details of the selection
shortcuts.endTable: Processes: end the selection, with confirmation
shortcuts.endDirect: Processes: end the selection without confirmation
shortcuts.clear: Clear selection; clear the process search first if one is active.
shortcuts.scrollSideways: With the pointer over a list, scroll sideways to the other columns
shortcuts.history: When the history chart has focus
shortcuts.time: Select the previous / next point in time
shortcuts.timeJump: Move backward / forward by a larger amount
shortcuts.timeFirst: Select the earliest point on the chart
shortcuts.latest: Go back to the latest readings and keep updating

mouse.hoverText: Show the readings and the processes at that time
mouse.clickText: Pin the cursor; when the curve shows averages, select the clicked span
mouse.rightText: Go back to the latest readings and keep updating
mouse.wheelText: Zoom the time range; while showing the latest readings, the right edge stays
mouse.shiftWheelText: Pan the time range and pause updates
mouse.navigatorText: Pan or zoom; this only pauses updates and never returns to the latest by itself
mouse.grip: Drag the handle left of a lane title
mouse.reading: Drag a reading onto the chart
mouse.readingText: Overlay it on a lane, or add a lane

hotkey.title: Show or hide Argus
hotkey.help: Press and release a key combination to save it. Esc cancels; Backspace turns the shortcut off.

done.off: The shortcut is turned off; turn it back on with the switch.

hint.order: Hold the modifiers (Ctrl, Alt, Shift or Win) first, then press the other key.
hint.multipleKeys: A global shortcut can have only one ordinary key.
hint.lockKey: Caps Lock, Num Lock and Scroll Lock aren't part of a combination and are ignored.
hint.maybeTaken: If nothing happens after pressing a combination, Windows or another app may be using it.

warning.common: {shortcut} has its own use in many apps. As a global shortcut, it will stop working there.
warning.inApp: {shortcut} switches pages or searches in Argus. As a global shortcut, it will no longer do that.
warning.imeSwitch: Ctrl+Space usually switches the input method. As a global shortcut, it will no longer do that.
warning.numpad: Keypad digits and the decimal point trigger the shortcut only while Num Lock is on.
warning.printScreen: {shortcut} may conflict with the Windows screenshot or a screenshot app.

error.invalid: {shortcut} can't be used as a shortcut: {reason}
error.taken: {shortcut} is in use by Windows or another app (possibly another running Argus). Choose a different combination.
error.saveFailed: Couldn't save the setting. The shortcut is unchanged.

issue.noKey: Modifier keys alone can't be a shortcut; add an ordinary key.
issue.unsupported: {key} can't be used in a global shortcut.
issue.lockKey: Caps Lock, Num Lock and Scroll Lock can't be part of a combination.
issue.needsModifier: A combination needs Ctrl, Alt or Win (except F13–F24 and Shift+F1–F11). Other Shift-only combinations would interfere with typing in every app.
issue.reserved: {shortcut} is used by Windows or by most apps.
issue.taskManager: Ctrl+Shift+Esc opens Task Manager. To have it open Argus, turn on “Replace Task Manager” in Settings → Permissions.
issue.editing: {shortcut} is used for copy, paste and other editing.

privilege.desc: Lets Argus running as a standard user manage system processes and services, and collect data that requires administrator permission.
privilege.statusDesc: Argus connects to the service automatically while it runs.

state.busy: Waiting for administrator permission or working on the service…
state.unknown: Can't read the status right now
state.unreachable: Running, but can't connect right now

privilege.outdated: Service version {service} doesn't match Argus {app}. Click Update service.
privilege.incompatible: Click Update service to install the version that matches Argus; Argus then connects to it.

install.title: Enable the privileged service?

uninstall.title: Uninstall the privileged service?
uninstall.body: Windows Task Manager is restored first, then the background service is stopped and removed. Actions on system processes and services are then limited by Argus's current permissions. Uninstalling requires administrator permission.

privilege.uninstalled: The privileged service has been uninstalled.

broken.repair: Click Repair service to reinstall the service files and reconnect, or click Uninstall to remove the leftover service registration. Both require administrator permission.
broken.remove: Click Uninstall to remove the leftover service registration; the service can then be installed again. Uninstalling requires administrator permission.
broken.notice: The privileged service is damaged and can't start. See Settings → Permissions.

privilege.deletePending: The service has been uninstalled. Windows finishes removing it once programs that show the service, such as the Services console, are closed; refresh the status to check. Restarting Windows also completes the removal.

repair.title: Repair the privileged service?
repair.body: The authorization record is lost, so the account that the service was authorized for can't be confirmed. Repairing reinstalls the service files and authorizes the service for the current Windows account; an enabled Task Manager replacement is first restored to Windows Task Manager.

taskManager.title: Replace Task Manager
taskManager.desc: Makes Ctrl+Shift+Esc and other Task Manager shortcuts open Argus.

confirm.title: Replace Task Manager?
confirm.body: Ctrl+Shift+Esc and other ways of opening Task Manager will open Argus. The change applies to the whole PC; other accounts still open Windows Task Manager. Turning it on requires administrator permission. If Argus fails to start, it attempts to open the built-in Task Manager. Keep the standalone recovery tool so the change can be undone if the interface or the service can't run.

taskManager.openNativeHint: Opens Windows Task Manager once and keeps the current replacement setting.
taskManager.openNativeFailed: Could not open Windows Task Manager: {error}
taskManager.restored: Windows Task Manager has been restored.
taskManager.retry: Refresh the status and try again.
taskManager.recovery: If the interface won't open, run the standalone recovery tool: {path}

window.title: Window transitions
window.desc: Fade the window when showing, hiding, minimizing or restoring it. Follows the Windows Animation effects setting by default.

ui.title: Interface animations
ui.desc: Page and dialog transitions, the sliding selection marker, and icon motion. Follows the Windows Animation effects setting by default.

chart.title: Chart animations
chart.desc: Higher frame rates make charts smoother but use more resources.

acceleration.title: Hardware acceleration
acceleration.desc: When off, the CPU draws the interface instead of the GPU, and CPU usage rises.

data.intervalDesc: Shorter intervals give finer charts but make Argus itself use more resources.

minimized.title: Refresh rate while minimized
minimized.desc: Longer intervals cost less in the background, but rules can take up to one interval to apply to newly started programs, and above 5 seconds history is recorded more sparsely.

tray.title: Refresh rate in the tray
tray.desc: Longer intervals cost less in the background, but rules can take up to one interval to apply to newly started programs, and above 5 seconds history is recorded more sparsely.

releaseHidden.title: Free memory when hidden
releaseHidden.desc: After the window has been minimized or in the tray for this long, Argus frees the memory its charts use. Reopening the window can then take a moment.

netUnit.title: Network speed unit
netUnit.desc: Bytes match the unit of disk speeds; bits match network adapter link speeds and broadband plans.

history.title: Record history
history.on: Usually records resource usage and the top processes every 5 seconds. The data stays on this PC.
history.off: Off. Existing records are still removed by the retention limits, or can be cleared now.

confirm.title: Clear history?
confirm.body: All recorded history ({size}) will be deleted. This can't be undone.

record.title: What to record
record.desc: Readings that need the privileged service are recorded once it is available.
record.alwaysDesc: Totals of CPU, memory, disks, network, GPU and battery
record.sensorsDesc: CPU temperature, core voltage, fan speeds and device temperatures
record.memoryDetailDesc: Committed, cached, compressed, paged and non-paged pool
record.disksDesc: Read and write rates, active time, average response time
record.processDiskDesc: Disk read and write rates of each recorded process
record.processNetworkDesc: Send and receive rates of each recorded process
record.processesDesc: More processes make range rankings more complete and records larger
record.estimate: With this selection, a full day of recording takes about {size}.

limit.title: Retention limits
limit.desc: With both set, the first limit reached applies; the oldest days are removed first.

estimate.one: With the current recording, about {count} day is kept ({by}, about {size}).
estimate.other: With the current recording, about {count} days are kept ({by}, about {size}).

limit.unbounded: With no limit on either, the history keeps growing.
limit.confirmBody: History beyond the new limit will be removed, oldest days first. This cannot be undone.

detail.title: Detail of older records
detail.mergedDesc: Merged days keep the average, peak and busiest processes of each minute at about one eighth of the size.

confirmBody.one: Records older than {count} day will be merged into one frame per minute, keeping only averages, peaks and the busiest processes. This cannot be undone.
confirmBody.other: Records older than {count} days will be merged into one frame per minute, keeping only averages, peaks and the busiest processes. This cannot be undone.

place.title: Location
place.records: Move the existing records ({size}) as well; otherwise recording starts afresh in the new location
place.pause: Recording pauses during the move and resumes afterwards.
place.moved: The history location has been changed.

rules.title: Set priority or efficiency mode when a program starts
rules.desc: Saved rules apply to running processes right away. Rules can also be added by right-clicking a process in the list and selecting Add rule.

summary.noAction: Choose a priority or efficiency mode to apply.
summary.notSeen: The program hasn't been detected yet.

denied.one: Access denied for {count} process; enable the privileged service, though protected processes may still be restricted
denied.other: Access denied for {count} processes; enable the privileged service, though protected processes may still be restricted

failed.one: Couldn't apply to {count} process; check the privileged service status, then save the rules again
failed.other: Couldn't apply to {count} processes; check the privileged service status, then save the rules again

detail.ready: Installing requires administrator permission. Argus exits during the installation and restarts when it's done.
detail.portable: The portable version doesn't update automatically. Download the new version from the release page.
detail.source: Updates come from GitHub Releases or the official Argus mirror. Argus verifies the installer signature before installation.

auto.title: Check for updates automatically
auto.desc: Checks once a day. New versions download in the background and are installed only after confirmation.

whatsNew.title: Show what's new after updating
whatsNew.desc: When off, only a notice in the bottom-right corner says that Argus was updated.

channel.label: Update channel
channel.desc: Beta gets new features earlier but may be less stable than Stable. After switching from Beta to Stable, Argus updates only once a stable version is newer than the current one.

route.label: Download source
route.desc: GitHub proxies are run by third parties and can see this PC's IP address and the files it downloads. Installers must pass signature and version checks.

proxy.label: GitHub proxy
proxy.fallback: If GitHub and the official mirror are unavailable, Argus tries this proxy, then the other built-in proxies.
proxy.only: All update requests go through this proxy.

custom.title: Custom proxy
custom.desc: A prefix added before GitHub URLs. It must use https, e.g. https://example.com/.
custom.label: Custom proxy URL

star.title: Star reminder
star.desc: Shows a card in the bottom-right corner of the window once a day, asking for a star on GitHub.

about.tagline: A fast, modern, information-rich Windows task manager.
about.service: Running as a standard user. The privileged service is connected and carries out actions that need administrator rights.
about.standard: Running as a standard user. Information and actions for some system processes are limited.

onboarding.title: Welcome guide
onboarding.desc: Go through the essential settings and tips again.

community.title: Feedback and community
community.desc: Join the QQ group {group} to report problems, suggest features or share experiences with other users (in Chinese).

channel.title: Telegram channel
channel.desc: Join the Telegram channel {channel} for release updates and project news.

license.title: License
license.desc: Argus is free software, released under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 or any later version (AGPL-3.0-or-later). It can be redistributed and modified under the terms of that license. Argus comes with no warranty.

notices.title: Third-party components
notices.desc: Open-source components included in Argus, with their licenses and copyright notices.

log.title: Log
log.desc: Diagnostic logs stay on this PC and omit command lines, credentials and file contents. Attach the log when reporting a problem; before sharing it publicly, check its paths for user names.

diagnostics.title: Diagnostic information
diagnostics.desc: Copy the current version, runtime state, hardware and display settings to paste into an issue report.

sensors.title: Kernel sensors
sensors.desc: Enable the privileged service first. Installing, updating or starting the PawnIO driver requires administrator permission. Turning this off stops Argus's kernel sensor collection and leaves the driver installed.
sensors.preparing: Preparing the driver. Complete the administrator prompt if shown; the first installation downloads a package.

administrator.development: Persistent administrator authorization is unavailable with development hot reload. Use a release build.
administrator.title: Run as administrator
administrator.desc: Authorize once to run Argus as administrator from sign-in, shortcuts, and Task Manager entry points.
administrator.restart: Argus restarts after switching, keeping settings and history.
administrator.afterOnboarding: Continue setup after authorizing. Argus restarts with the selected permissions when setup finishes.
administrator.standardAccount: This account has no administrator identity, so automatic administrator startup is unavailable. The privileged service can perform supported administrative actions.

appearance.scaleDesc: Resize text, icons and controls from 80% to 150%.
appearance.fontDesc: Base font size: 11–20 px. Headings and secondary text scale proportionally.
appearance.saveFailed: Could not save interface preferences. Check that the configuration folder is writable.

leaks.title: Resource leak alerts
leaks.desc: Marks programs on the Processes page that appear to leak handles or processes.
